**English** · 简体中文
# dsh-session-send
A session bus for DSH: lets **independent DSH sessions / agents send messages to each other** and wa
ke each other up — no human copying prompts between windows.

Modelled on the *approach* of OpenClaw's `session send`, built as a DSH plugin.
**Off by default.**
It only takes effect inside a project you explicitly enable.
> **This is not an OpenClaw plugin.** It runs inside the DSH host and **never reads or writes `openc

law.json`**,
> does not read OpenClaw's session ledger, and registers no channel. What it borrows is

the *message semantics*,
> not OpenClaw's configuration or data plane.
## Message semantics (aligned with openclaw `session send`)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### The point: the message actually wakes the other session
This is not "write to a database and hope someone polls it". When the target is a live DSH session,

the message goes straight into **that session's own inbox** and wakes it — the same behaviour as
ope
nclaw's `session send`.
| openclaw `mode` | this plugin `deliveryMode` | DSH call | behaviour |

| `notify` | `notify` | `agent.inject(msg)` | deposit only, no wake |
| `steer` | `steer` (default)

| `agent.steer(msg)` | inject into the running turn at the next step boundary, and wake |
| `followu
p` | `followup` | `agent.followup(msg)` | queue as the next turn, and wake |

The host implementation of `agent.steer()` is `this.inbox.splice(target, Infinity, 0, [message])`
pl
us `wakeDriver()` — it appends directly to the target session's own inbox with **no parent/child che

ck**.
That is why N independent, peer-level sessions can message each other freely; nobody has to be
independent, peer-level sessions can message each other freely; nobody has to be anyone's subagent.
### When the target is not in this process
The message is still persisted. It is delivered when the target session is opened again, and can be

read with `dsh_bus_inbox`. Delivery never silently drops a message: a missing target raises
`E_TARGE
T_NOT_FOUND`, an ambiguous one raises `E_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`.

## Typical use: several sessions sharing one project

You have a project split across several sessions — pipeline, chapter runner, gate, and so on.
One se
ssion discovers it needs another to continue. Instead of asking a human to carry the prompt over:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The gate session wakes up, reads the message, and starts working.
## How the project root is resolved
**Resolved per call, from the caller** — never pinned at mount time.
Priority: explicit config `projectRoot` > the calling session's `cwd` > current initiator's `cwd` >
icit config `projectRoot` > the calling session's `cwd` > current initiator's `cwd` > process `cwd`.

Why it has to work this way: the host is long-lived and holds sessions from several workspaces.
Whic
hever session happened to trigger mounting at startup must not decide which project's config every l

ater call reads —
otherwise a session in project A would send messages using project B's enable swit

r call reads —
otherwise a session in project A would send messages using project B's enable switch.
A real bug this fixed: at startup `currentInitiator()` is empty, so the root fell back to `process.c

wd()`
(the profile directory). Every later call then looked for `.dsh-bus.json` there and reported
"
project not enabled" even though the real project had one.
## Enabling a project (no hand-editing)

Open the **Session row's "..." menu** in the left sidebar and click the bus entry.
It writes `<works

pace>/.dsh-bus.json` and takes effect immediately; click again to turn it off.
The menu shows the cu
rrent state (on / off) for that session's project.
Only one file is ever written, and only its `enabled` field:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A corrupt config is never overwritten — the plugin refuses and reports why.
### Why the switch lives on the Session row, not the project row

`ui-workspace`'s project-row menu is a hardcoded `[rename, delete]` with no extension slot.
The sess
ion row does have one, so the switch lives there and acts on **that session's project**.
## Configurable fields
| field | default | notes |

| `enabled` | `false` | per-project switch |
| `transport.kind` | `'sqlite'` | `sqlite` / `file` / `

in-process` |
| `registry.sources` | `['dsh-team','dsh-sessions']` | which registries to expose |
|

`registry.stateDir` | `'.agent-teams'` | dsh-team state directory name |
| `registry.requireRegistra

tion` | `true` | unregistered sessions are invisible and unaddressable |
[该节后续省略]
### What may be used as a `to` target
| valid `to` | notes |

| **session id** | unique, stable, never changes — **the reliable key** |
| registered name | bound

to the session id |
| config `labels` name | bound to the session id |
| host title | a real host fi

eld |
| `"*"` | broadcast to other sessions in this project |

**The fallback label (`11-08 15:49 · e9f8dca`) is NOT addressable.**
It is a *derived* display strin

g built from the id and its creation time, not an identity.
Treating it as a key would let a derived

value impersonate an identity, and it would break the
moment the display format changed. It exists

for humans to tell rows apart — use the session id
(or have the target register a name) when you act

to tell rows apart — use the session id
(or have the target register a name) when you actually send.
## Known limitations

**An inactive session cannot be reliably woken.** A session that is not currently loaded in the
host

process (`status: "inactive"` in `dsh_bus_agents`) can be cold-started with
`agentLoop.resume`, and

the message does reach its queue — but the host will not drive that resumed
agent through a turn on

its own. The message is delivered when the session next becomes active.
For immediate wake-up the t
arget must be `live` (opened in the UI at least once).
This is host behaviour, not something the plugin can work around. `deliveries[0].detail` says which
of the two happened.
**Hot reload cannot replace routes or modules.** DSH's ESM cache and the duplicate-exact-route guard
mean code changes need a host restart; the plugin itself supports hot re-mount for config changes.
